question: What primary form of energy is utilized by MRI to generate diagnostic images?
explanation: MRI combines a strong magnetic field with radiofrequency waves to manipulate hydrogen protons and produce detailed images. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T12#GNS123_U2_T12_h1)

question: Why is MRI preferred over standard computed tomography when imaging soft tissue structures like the spinal cord?

options.A: It delivers a lower financial cost to the hospital
options.B: It provides superior differentiation of soft tissue detail
options.C: It requires zero preparation or patient screening
options.D: It operates significantly faster in emergency scenarios

explanation: The interaction of magnetic fields and hydrogen protons yields exceptional contrast resolution, making soft tissues far easier to visualize than on standard X-ray-based scans. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T12#GNS123_U2_T12_h1)

question: Which atomic nucleus is primarily targeted during a standard clinical MRI scan?
explanation: Because the human body has a high water content, hydrogen protons are abundant and highly responsive to magnetic manipulation. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T12#GNS123_U2_T12_h2)

question: What physical event occurs immediately after the radiofrequency pulse is turned off during an MRI scan?

options.A: Tissue temperature rises significantly due to friction
options.B: Protons permanently stop spinning within the tissue
options.C: The primary magnetic field shuts down automatically
options.D: Protons release energy as they return to alignment

explanation: Relaxation is the process where protons realign with the main magnetic field, emitting radio signals that the scanner captures to build the image. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T12#GNS123_U2_T12_h2)

question: Which clinical condition is MRI exceptionally sensitive for detecting in its earliest stages?
explanation: Diffusion-weighted MRI can identify ischemic changes in brain tissue within minutes of a stroke onset, far quicker than standard computed tomography. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T12#GNS123_U2_T12_h3)

question: A patient with a suspected ligamentous knee injury is sent for imaging. Why is MRI chosen over a routine X-ray?

options.A: MRI takes less than thirty seconds to complete in outpatient clinics
options.B: X-rays expose the patient to massive doses of radioactive material
options.C: X-rays cannot visualize any part of the lower extremity
options.D: MRI clearly displays soft tissues like cartilage and ligaments

explanation: Routine X-rays primarily capture dense bone structures, whereas MRI excels at imaging soft tissue components like menisci and ligaments. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T12#GNS123_U2_T12_h3)

question: When is the primary magnetic field of an MRI machine active?

options.A: Only during the actual image acquisition phase
options.C: Only after the radiologist injects contrast dye
options.D: Only when the computer workstation is turned on

explanation: Superconducting magnets remain fully energized at all times, making the scanning room a permanent magnetic hazard zone. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T12#GNS123_U2_T12_h4)

question: Why must a nurse screen a patient for a history of working with metal before an MRI scan?

options.A: Metal fragments interfere with the hospital's electrical grid
options.B: Unnoticed metallic splinters in the eye can shift and cause blindness
options.C: Any metallic trace causes the contrast dye to become toxic
options.D: Retained metal automatically shuts down the cooling system

explanation: Ferromagnetic fragments lodged in sensitive areas like the eye can move or heat up when exposed to the magnetic field, causing severe tissue damage. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T12#GNS123_U2_T12_h4)

question: Which of the following is considered an absolute contraindication for an MRI scan?

options.C: A history of mild seasonal allergies
options.D: A healed tibia fracture with internal plates

explanation: Traditional pacemakers contain metallic components and circuitry that malfunction or displace in a strong magnetic field, posing a life-threatening hazard. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T12#GNS123_U2_T12_h5)

question: Nephrogenic systemic fibrosis is a severe medical complication linked to the administration of which substance in vulnerable patients?
explanation: Patients with severe renal impairment can develop nephrogenic systemic fibrosis when exposed to gadolinium contrast agents used to enhance MRI clarity. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T12#GNS123_U2_T12_h5)

question: What is the primary reason for securing a patient's position with cushions and instructing them not to move during an MRI?

options.A: To prevent the patient from falling off the narrow table
options.B: To ensure the contrast dye circulates evenly
options.C: To prevent motion artifact from blurring the images
options.D: To keep the patient's heart rate artificially lowered

explanation: Patient movement disrupts the spatial encoding of signals, resulting in blurry, diagnostically useless scans that must be repeated. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T12#GNS123_U2_T12_h6)

question: A patient expresses alarm over the loud, rhythmic knocking sounds coming from the scanner during the procedure. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Immediately halt the scan because the machine is malfunctioning
options.B: Remove the patient from the room to check for equipment damage
options.C: Reassure the patient that this loud acoustic noise is completely normal
options.D: Administer an emergency dose of intravenous muscle relaxants

explanation: The knocking sounds are produced by gradient coils rapidly switching electrical currents during imaging, which is an expected part of operation. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T12#GNS123_U2_T12_h6)

question: What primary instruction should be given to a patient who received gadolinium contrast during an outpatient MRI?

options.A: Take a strong diuretic medication immediately upon returning home
options.B: Avoid eating dairy products for the rest of the day
options.C: Maintain high fluid intake to help clear the contrast agent
options.D: Remain on bed rest for the next twenty-four hours

explanation: Encouraging fluids helps the kidneys excrete the gadolinium contrast efficiently, reducing retention time in the body. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T12#GNS123_U2_T12_h7)

question: A patient who received procedural sedation for severe claustrophobia during an MRI is ready for discharge. Which assessment finding is most crucial before sending them home?

options.A: Their vital signs have returned to baseline and they can walk steadily
options.B: They remember every detail of the imaging procedure
options.C: They have completely finished a heavy meal
options.D: Their blood glucose level is within the normal fasting range

explanation: Sedatives impair motor coordination and respiratory drive, requiring stable vital signs and safe ambulation before unsupervised discharge. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T12#GNS123_U2_T12_h7)
